items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Stecklet Interview, 1959-06-15
items.q: I can get you done with J.C. Hall, the resident engineer. I said, well, all right. He said, go down and see him. He said, you can see him there pressing the river. And he says, he'll entertain you. So he asked me whether I was a first class man.

ctx.x: What was your first instrument that you took up? Did you start? Cornet. You started right on cornet.

Yes, sir. And I made a crackerjack, if I have to say it myself. I'm not given to post him, but I'm telling you what's a fact. And so, we had, we, we used to rehearse in my daddy's kitchen. He had a very big kitchen, you know, it was, I believe, 20 feet long, by 16 or 18 feet wide. Now, he says, during the winter months, he says, that's where you all live. So he decided to make a big kitchen, you see. And that's where we used to rehearse, at mine, at 3817 Dauphine Street, in my daddy's home. And he used to get a…
Well, I was wondering some more about this American brass band.
